criteria.criterion: The stated objective is implemented: Show me, for one engineering job, every developer attempt that was made and what each one cost, so I can tell whether an automated run is converging or thrashing without reading the whole history.
criteria.evidence_ref: company/engineering/attempt_ledger.py:71-157 — build_attempt_ledger joins three stores into AttemptLedger with per-attempt entries and aggregates

criteria.criterion: company-engineering-execution invariant still holds: The authorized work order is immutable; every later stage carries its fingerprint and refuses a mismatch.
criteria.evidence_ref: company/engineering/attempt_ledger.py — read-only projection, no store writes, no fingerprint mutation

criteria.criterion: company-engineering-execution invariant still holds: A review outcome is the worst of the attested and deterministic verdicts, so a reviewer PASS cannot rescue a failed check.
criteria.evidence_ref: diff.patch — no changes to company/engineering/review.py or adjudicate()

criteria.criterion: company-engineering-execution invariant still holds: The implementer and the reviewer are different employees, routed by disjoint capabilities.
criteria.evidence_ref: diff.patch — no changes to routing logic in orchestrator.py

criteria.criterion: company-engineering-execution invariant still holds: The protected governance surface is digested before the work and re-read at review; a change blocks the job.
criteria.evidence_ref: diff.patch — no changes to company/engineering/protected.py or governance digest code

criteria.criterion: company-engineering-execution invariant still holds: No state means approved and nothing merges, deploys or publishes; the CEO decision is recorded, not acted on.
criteria.evidence_ref: company/engineering/attempt_ledger.py:1-13 — docstring declares read-only; no store write calls in the module

criteria.criterion: company-engineering-execution invariant still holds: The gate verdict is read from the gate's own report; this subsystem holds no code that can produce one.

findings.summary: attempt_ledger.py imports Mapping (line 18), Outcome (line 23) and JobState (line 28) but never uses any of them.
Usage-to-attempt correlation assumes records appear in 1-based sequence order; the implementer disclosed this and the stores use sorted_records(), so it holds today but is implicit.

notes: Purely additive: one new module, re-export in __init__.py, four new tests. No existing behaviour was modified. The three unused imports are harmless but worth cleaning. The sequence-correlation assumption is documented by the implementer and sound given sorted_records(), but a future store migration should be aware of it.
